This is a lesson on one bass line the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Motown: root, fifth, octave**. It is built up from 2 simpler patterns, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read what the band will play on the staff underneath: the whole pass is written out when Play starts, before it sounds. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd) · [Bass lines](index.qmd#bass)

## The pattern

A two-bar line: the root on 1 and the and of 2, the fifth on 3, then the octave and fifth in eighths; the second bar ends by leading into the next chord. A plain stand-in for a Motown bass part, which would move far more.

It belongs in *Motown / soul*. Here it is in the motown / soul style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="motown" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="112" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass drums" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"Motown: root, fifth, octave","opts":{"bassFeel":"motown"}}]'></div>

## Step 1: Root and fifth

Start with something simpler. The boom of boom-chick: the root on beat 1 and the fifth on beat 3, short, the same every bar. In 3/4 it is one note a bar, root one bar and fifth the next.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](bass-alt.qmd) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="motown" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="78" data-on="bass drums" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Root and fifth","opts":{"bassFeel":"alt"}}]'></div>

## Step 2: Dotted (1, and of 2, 3)

The root on beat 1, again on the and of 2 and on beat 3, the same rhythm as the kick drum. Every second bar ends with an eighth note that leads into the next chord.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](bass-dotted.qmd) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="motown" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="78" data-on="bass drums" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Dotted (1, and of 2, 3)","opts":{"bassFeel":"dotted"}}]'></div>

## Step 3: Motown: root, fifth, octave, slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** A two-bar line. The first bar is the dotted rhythm with the fifth on beat 3, then octave and fifth in eighths. The second bar leads by step into the next chord. Play it lightly and short; a Motown bass part bounces.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="motown" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="78" data-on="bass drums" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"Motown: root, fifth, octave","opts":{"bassFeel":"motown"}},{"label":"Dotted (1, and of 2, 3) (the step before)","opts":{"bassFeel":"dotted"}}]'></div>

## Step 4: Up to tempo, with the band

The whole band, at 112 beats a minute. Play along, then switch the band's bass off and take the part yourself.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="motown" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="112" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass drums" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"Motown: root, fifth, octave","opts":{"bassFeel":"motown"}}]'></div>

## Step 5: Two chords in a bar

Harder: now some bars have two chords, two beats each. Each chord gets its root when it arrives; the pattern squeezes into the beats it has.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="motown" data-chart="C Am|F G|C Am|F G" data-tempo="112" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="bass" data-choice-label="Bass line:" data-choices='[{"label":"Motown: root, fifth, octave","opts":{"bassFeel":"motown"}}]'></div>
